Content:
I've never seen anyone else figure out my special hot dog recipe, so I will drop it here:

Get some pulled pork, pre-made store bought is fine. Drop that in a skillet with your hot dog. Grill the hot dog, crisp up the pulled pork. 

Assemble the hot dog in a bun, pile the crispy pulled pork on top, cheddar cheese on that, a line of BBQ sauce over that. Put the whole thing under the broiler to melt the cheese, and enjoy. You will lose a couple years off the end of your life, but it's worth it.

Author: @mndlessdrwer
Content:
Pro tip if you've got one of those 4th burner pots that are tall and narrow, you can fill it up with oil and drop your spiralized hotdog into it, skewer and all, and fry it until crispy and delicious. Then just remove it from the skewer into a footlong bun and enjoy with some mustard, chili, and slaw for an impeccable hotdog experience.

On a side note: if you're going to drop a lot of money on a new grill, consider one of the models from Solaire, like their 42" infrared grill model. I'm not a spokesperson, just someone with a strong affinity toward the relatively uncommon ceramic honeycomb infrared grill burner design who is annoyed that more companies haven't tried to make a grill with just that type of burner. For about 75% of grilling tasks, using such a burner design will result in a vastly superior cooking experience with less propane wasted, since the infrared ceramic honeycomb burner design results in significantly more efficient combustion, added heat from radiant infrared conversion, and a more even distribution of heat due to the larger surface area of the burner design. If you don't often grill large quantities of food and don't want to invest in a large and cumbersome grill, you can purchase one of their camping or tailgating grills that are sold on Amazon. This kind of grill burner is particularly excellent when grilling steaks, fish, or anything else with a large surface area that benefits from extremely high heat.

Author: @awwpoosnax
Content: My perfect hotdog recipe: Diamond cut a hotdog not all the way through (diagonal cuts down the length of the dog, repeat on the opposite diagonal creating a diamond pattern. This creates max surface area). Separately, mix a 2:1 ratio of spicy brown mustard (I prefer Gulden's) and dark brown sugar. Roll the hot dog in the sauce, ensuring as much gets into the crevices of the diamond patter as possible. Air fryer the dog at 350°F for 6-10 minutes, or until the sauce has begun to caramelize. While the dog is cooking, butter and toast the insides of the bun. When all is read, assemble and enjoy!
